h1: Lean vs Six Sigma: Key Differences and When to Use Each
seo_title: Lean vs Six Sigma: Key Differences and When to Use Each
meta_description: Lean vs Six Sigma compared: waste vs variation, tools, metrics and Lean Six Sigma, with a worked claims example and a simple rule for choosing.
excerpt: Lean removes waste and waiting; Six Sigma reduces variation and defects. A side-by-side comparison, a mean-or-spread rule for choosing, and one claims process analysed with both lenses.
parent_topic_cluster: Quality and process improvement (Lean / Six Sigma)
learning_objectives: Explain the difference between Lean and Six Sigma in terms of the problem each targets
Choose a starting approach using the mean-or-spread rule against a customer requirement
Calculate lead time with Little's Law, process cycle efficiency, DPMO, sigma level and first-pass yield for one process
Describe how Lean tools sit inside the DMAIC phases of Lean Six Sigma
Recognise when each approach is unsuitable and what to use instead

formulas.formula: Little's Law: WIP = throughput x lead time (equivalently lead time = WIP / throughput)
formulas.variables: WIP in claims; throughput in claims per working day; lead time in working days; stable process assumed
both in working days; result as %

formulas.formula: Average evidence wait = share complete x 2 days + share second request x 10 days
Rework minutes per day = throughput x share defective x 45 min
